entityDescription:
Apricot Studio is the trading name of Jonathan Kerr Technology Ltd, a United Kingdom company developing resilient position, navigation and timing (PNT) technology for small uncrewed aircraft systems, with engineering based in Edinburgh.
The company's core product, Octant, is a low-SWaP companion module that maintains an aircraft's position, velocity and attitude estimate when GNSS is unavailable, degraded, jammed or spoofed. It fuses a global-shutter camera with an inertial measurement unit (visual-inertial odometry) on commodity CPU hardware, requiring no GPU, and streams the resulting navigation solution to standard autopilots over the MAVLink protocol so that it can be integrated into existing airframes rather than requiring a purpose-built platform.
The distinguishing capability is navigation integrity: the module publishes a quantified confidence and health signal alongside every pose estimate, enabling an aircraft to detect and respond to degradation in its own navigation solution instead of acting on an unreliable position.
Capabilities: visual-inertial odometry, multi-sensor fusion, navigation integrity monitoring, embedded real-time software (C++, ROS 2), simulation-based validation, and flight-test hardware integration.
Current maturity: validated in closed-loop simulation and against public benchmark datasets, with flight-hardware testing underway.

entityDescription:
One man company (Alain BENOIT), providing consultancy services to space entities.
Large experience in Space Systems procurement, including ITT preparations and evaluations, Phase A to E reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, QAR) for Earth Observation, Telecom, Science, Exploration missions and space vehicles and launchers.
Strong expertise in System and AOCS/GNC engineering and verification, sensors and actuators development, dynamic analyses for Active Debris Removal missions. 
Alain BENOIT devoted most of his career to the Technical Management of AOCS teams, first in the European space industry and then at ESA/ESTEC. 
In 2004, he was appointed Head of the Control Systems Division, in charge of AOCS and GNC support to ESA projects and associated sensors technology development. 
He took an active role in the development of the Control Branch ECSS E60 and in SAVOIR initiative. 
In parallel, he supported ESA satellites reviews and tenders evaluations as chairman of Technical Panels at system and satellite level.
In 2019, he became Senior Advisor in the Earth Observation Directorate of ESA and contributed to the preparation of the Copernicus Expansion Satellites procurement. Since May 2021, he is retired from ESA and remains active in his field of expertise through consultancy contracts.

entityDescription:
CERMAT is a Polish SME specialising in advanced technical ceramics and precision surface finishing. The company manufactures and machines components from alumina (Al₂O₃), zirconia-toughened alumina (ZTA), zirconia (ZrO₂), silicon carbide (SiC) and sintered carbides, serving industrial customers across Poland and the EU.
Core competencies include precision lapping and polishing of ceramic components down to sub-micron flatness, diamond grinding, cutting-edge geometry for ceramic and carbide tools, and dimensional metrology to ISO 1101 (CMM-based flatness, parallelism and coaxiality verification). The company operates its own production and finishing facility, including flat lapping equipment for components up to 600 mm, and provides dye-penetrant inspection of ceramic parts.
The company additionally offers ceramic additive manufacturing (vat photopolymerisation / DLP) of alumina components, covering the full process chain from green-body printing through debinding and sintering to post-sinter precision grinding and lapping of functional surfaces — enabling complex geometries such as thin-walled (0.5 mm) monolithic parts, internal channels and near-net-shape components with machined datum surfaces.

entityDescription:
LoreSpace develops decision-support software for spacecraft systems engineering, based on a formal Space Systems Engineering Ontology in OWL/RDF aligned with ECSS practice and the spacecraft lifecycle (Phases A–F).
The system ingests programme artefacts — system and subsystem requirements, interface control documents, verification matrices, test and anomaly records — and connects them into a programme knowledge graph. Engineers query the graph in natural language and receive evidence-backed, cited answers; the system generates and maintains engineering artefacts from the same model, providing digital continuity across organisational and disciplinary boundaries in model-based system approaches.
Capabilities: ontology and knowledge-model development; requirements and verification traceability; automated change-impact and variant-delta analysis; configuration management support; document-to-graph ingestion pipelines; SPARQL/SHACL validation; agentic workflow automation over programme data.
LoreSpace AB is a Swedish company based in Stockholm, incubated at ESA BIC Sweden.

entityDescription:
Quantum Valley Ideas Lab (QVIL) is a not-for-profit advanced technology R&D organization based in Waterloo, focused on accelerating the development and commercialization of quantum technologies. Its mission is to generate high-value IP, create globally competitive companies, and deliver economic, societal, and national security benefits for Canada.

Founded in 2016, QVIL has become one of Canada’s leading applied quantum R&D organizations, building the infrastructure and capabilities needed to accelerate the research and development of quantum sensing technologies.

QVIL operates a focused portfolio model, advancing multiple high-impact projects at a time to translate scientific breakthroughs into deployable technologies and commercialization opportunities. The organization has built a multidisciplinary team of over 40 researchers and engineers with expertise spanning atomic physics, photonics, nanofabrication, and systems engineering. QVIL has developed more than 50 patent families and advanced multiple quantum sensing technologies, including world-leading capabilities in radio frequency sensing, with applications across defence, telecommunications, and advanced industrial sectors.

QVIL maintains active collaborations with more than 20 partners across defence, aerospace, telecommunications, and academia, and has engagements with multiple Canadian. These collaborations support technology validation, system integration, and alignment with real-world operational requirements.

entityDescription: SUPCO (Sustainable Urban Planning Consultants) is a Greek consulting and engineering firm specialising in urban and spatial planning, sustainable development, geospatial analysis, environmental assessment and project management. The company provides services to public and private sector clients and has extensive experience in Local and Special Urban Plans, carrying capacity assessments, sustainable tourism, climate-neutral urban development and European programmes. SUPCO integrates Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Earth Observation and satellite-derived data, Artificial Intelligence and advanced spatial analysis into planning and decision-support applications. Its expertise also includes land-use and land-cover monitoring, environmental and socio-economic indicator assessment, biodiversity, climate resilience and the localisation of the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The company develops Web GIS platforms and digital spatial-data tools and operates under certified management systems including ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 50001 and ISO 37001.

entityDescription: StratoChaser develops small- to medium-scale High-Altitude Platforms for stratospheric operation at 15–35 km. The platform is a reusable balloon-glider hybrid designed for fully autonomous operations across the complete cycle — launch, flight, recovery and relaunch — without dedicated launch infrastructure, ground segment build-out or heavy logistics. It is being developed as a carrier for remote sensing, Earth observation and passive RF/EM monitoring payloads, addressing use cases that fall between airborne and satellite assets in persistence, revisit time and cost.

entityDescription:
Founded in 1851, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia (CCIS) stands as the largest independent, voluntary, and non-profit association of businesses in Slovenia. Representing more than 5,200 member companies spanning all sizes, sectors, and regions, CCIS serves as the central pillar of the nation's private sector. Its member network generates approximately 50% of the Slovenian economy's total gross value added and accounts for two-thirds of all foreign sales, making it the country's most influential business network.
As a primary hub for economic growth and international exchange, CCIS acts as a key gateway for business integration and market expansion in Slovenia. The organization operates as a dynamic networking megahub that facilitates the exchange of best practices, connects foreign investors with local enterprises, and links businesses to an extensive ecosystem of professionals both domestically and internationally.
Through its broad institutional reach and deep domain expertise, CCIS provides vital strategic support to the business community. It offers access to comprehensive market data, expert consulting, and key industry databases, delivering high-quality business intelligence on market actors, trends, and commercial opportunities across Slovenia.
